hunt.justification: Adversaries use the inherent trust in commerce and SaaS infrastructure to bypass standard email authentication. A negative result confirms that these trusted delivery pipelines are not currently being used to deliver social-engineering lures to the estate.

meta.name: Platform-as-a-Proxy Phishing and Input Abuse

related.reason: This hunt focuses specifically on platform proxy abuse; broader phishing hunts cover general lure types.

meta.analysis: A static detection rule on Staples or Dell order domains would create excessive noise. This hunt uses a gated flow to baseline normal brand activity first, then uses an agent to correlate lure keywords in cloud audit logs with registration patterns, identifying the specific 'Platform-as-a-Proxy' tradecraft that single-surface rules miss.

stages.name: Exploitation of Public-Facing Application Forms
observables: hostile string injected into name fields
malicious strings in company or title registration fields

stages.name: High-Reputation Notification Phishing
observables: Here’s your Staples order #9939818875. Thanks for shopping with us.
We have your order | Dell Purchase ID: 2009829958247
Call Our Sales Team in billing fields

stages.name: Abuse of Mail Delivery Status Reports
observables: Delivery status notification (DSN) with encapsulated phishing link
WeTransfer file-sharing lure inside administrative mail wrapper

scenario.summary: Adversaries are exploiting unvalidated input fields on legitimate SaaS and commerce platforms to inject malicious content into automated, high-reputation notifications. These 'Platform-as-a-Proxy' (PaaP) attacks leverage trusted infrastructure like Staples, Dell, and WeTransfer to deliver phishing lures, fake helplines, and fraudulent delivery status reports that bypass traditional email security filters.

meta.rationale: The hunt begins by identifying hosts running Microsoft 365, Office, or Cisco software. These systems are most relevant for phishing delivery and potential input abuse into corporate-facing applications.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using trusted third-party retail or SaaS infrastructure to deliver social-engineering lures by injecting fraudulent helpline numbers into transactional notification fields or abusing public-facing registration forms.

scope_hosts.description: Optional list of hosts identified in the scoping step; leave empty to hunt across the entire estate.

brand_domains.description: High-reputation domains identified in the report as being abused.

references.name: Talos — Parasitizing trust: How legitimate infrastructure becomes a delivery pipeline for attackers

nodes.label: Identify hosts with collaboration and mail software

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%microsoft 365%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%office%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%cisco%')
config.description: Find the hosts running Microsoft 365, Office, or Cisco components that could be the recipients of high-reputation phishing or the origin of form abuse.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts running products named in the threat research. These represent the likely targets for notification-based social engineering.

primitive_config.label: Identify hosts with collaboration and mail software
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, vendor_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%microsoft 365%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%office%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%cisco%')
primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts running products named in the threat research. These represent the likely targets for notification-based social engineering.

nodes.label: DNS lookups to abused brand domains

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) AS lookup_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{brand_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name
config.description: Identify hosts interacting with the specific Staples and Dell domains named in the report as a low-cost lead.
config.expected_signal: Hosts resolving the order-related domains. While frequent for shoppers, lookups coinciding with lure keywords in other surfaces suggest the receipt of a fraudulent notification.

primitive_config.label: DNS lookups to abused brand domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) AS lookup_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{brand_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name
primitive_config.expected: Hosts resolving the order-related domains. While frequent for shoppers, lookups coinciding with lure keywords in other surfaces suggest the receipt of a fraudulent notification.

config.objective: Review the DNS lookup volume and requesting processes. Identify hosts where lookups to order domains are rare or appear in tight clusters suggesting automated notifications.
config.description: Determine if the DNS activity is sufficiently anomalous or volume-heavy to justify expensive cloud and web queries.
config.expected_signal: A judgement on which hosts warrant deeper investigation based on their interaction with Staples or Dell infrastructure.
config.success_criteria: A verdict per host indicating whether the lead is worth following.

config.question: the eval-lead verdict identifies at least one host resolving abused brand domains in a suspicious manner
config.condition: the eval-lead verdict identifies at least one host resolving abused brand domains in a suspicious manner
config.description: Route the hunt to expensive searches only when a suspicious lead is confirmed.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, api_operation, resource_name, resource_uid, time FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE provider = 'm365' AND (instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'helpline') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'order confirmed') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'purchase id') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'wetransfer') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'non-delivery') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'delivery status') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Search Office 365 Unified Audit Logs for incoming mail items containing the specific report lures in the subject line.
config.expected_signal: Audit records reflecting the arrival of mail items with suspicious subjects like Helpline or Order Confirmed. M365 UAL captures subject lines in resource_name for certain Exchange operations.

primitive_config.label: M365 notification and lure activity
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, api_operation, resource_name, resource_uid, time FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE provider = 'm365' AND (instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'helpline') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'order confirmed') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'purchase id') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'wetransfer') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'non-delivery') > 0 OR instr(LOWER(resource_name), 'delivery status') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Audit records reflecting the arrival of mail items with suspicious subjects like Helpline or Order Confirmed. M365 UAL captures subject lines in resource_name for certain Exchange operations.

nodes.label: Platform registration and form input abuse

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, url_full, http_method, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE http_method = 'POST' AND (LOWER(url_path) LIKE '%signup%' OR LOWER(url_path) LIKE '%register%' OR LOWER(url_path) LIKE '%profile%') AND (LOWER(url_query) LIKE '%crypto%' OR LOWER(url_query) LIKE '%helpline%' OR LOWER(url_query) LIKE '%bitcoin%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find outbound web requests attempting to use registration forms with hostile strings, representing the input stage of the proxy abuse.
config.expected_signal: POST requests to registration or signup endpoints that contain crypto or helpline keywords in the query parameters. This indicates a host may be attempting to trigger reflexive notifications.

config.objective: Determine if a host has received a suspicious retail notification (from Staples/Dell) or if a host is attempting to inject lures into SaaS forms. Correlate the timing of DNS lookups to Staples/Dell with the arrival of mail items identified in the M365 logs.
config.description: Weigh the evidence from the DNS lead, the mail logs, and the HTTP traffic to confirm if Platform-as-a-Proxy abuse is occurring.
config.expected_signal: A detailed verdict citing mail arrivals, brand domain lookups, and form submissions per host.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign citing specific rows.

config.question: the final-triage verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the final-triage verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.description: Isolate high-risk hosts where social engineering lures have likely been delivered and engaged.
Contain the threat by preventing further interaction with the fraudulent notification or the attacker-controlled phone number.
config.instructions: Isolate the identified host. Revoke the M365 user session to prevent further engagement with fraudulent mail content.

config.description: Manually inspect the notification content and verify the fraud attempt.
config.instructions: Review the specific Exchange mail items found in the UAL. Check for the helpline numbers mentioned in the Talos report (806-283-7712 or 808-232-6397). Confirm if the user has made any outbound calls or browser connections to the retail brands immediately after receiving these notifications.

config.description: Finalize the hunt and document findings or false positives.
config.instructions: Record the examined hosts. If lookups to Staples/Dell were found but no lures were identified in mail logs, mark as benign retail activity. Document any new registration forms abused to update the HTTP keyword list.
